progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: C2: equal opposing rates versus amounts, closed versus insulated systems and the declared one-to-one A/B model. Entry check: equal rates need not mean equal concentrations. Rate and concentration are reminded in speech; released/absorbed heat and the enthalpy sign are explained here before use.
progression.startsWith: Established equilibrium, briefly add/remove one participating form at fixed temperature/volume and reclose. A/B is a well-mixed one-to-one first-order model with positive fixed coefficients and no side reactions. Separate temperature case: closed, fixed-volume 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g), forward heat-releasing.
progression.stopsAfter: Distinguish immediate imposed change from subsequent reaction, explain direction and fixed-temperature versus temperature-dependent K; diagnose possible open-oven water loss. No pressure/volume disturbance, catalyst mechanism, Q, ICE, K-expression construction or practical conduct.
progression.nextLesson: chem-m5-c04: gaseous volume/pressure and catalyst distinctions. C5 constructs equilibrium expressions; C6 calculations; C9 temperature/K data; p01 supervised named investigations remain separate.

selectedIntegrations.label: Biology: flowering plants
selectedIntegrations.status: Exact silent source/model and sampled native pass. Working animations integrated; fresh narration and later review remain pending.

progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: reproduction connects generations; cells contain inherited information in DNA; gametes are reproductive cells; sexual reproduction involves fusion of gametes, while asexual reproduction does not. Basic root, stem and leaf vocabulary helps with a runner. `bio-m5-b01` is the canonical prerequisite. Its selected draft provides the fusion criterion and a strawberry runner example; it is support material, not a presumed public upload. The animal contribution `bio-m5-b02a` is preceding playlist context, but its internal/external classification and chromosome-set model are not prerequisites for the plant explanation.
progression.startsWith: one strawberry plant can produce a new plant from a runner. A self-compatible flowering plant can also supply both gametes in a sexual reproductive event. One visible parent does not settle the classification.
progression.stopsAfter: the learner can explain pollen transfer, pollen-tube delivery and sperm-egg fusion in the supplied flowering-plant model; distinguish zygote-to-embryo development from ovule-to-seed development; explain strawberry runner propagation without fusion; classify supplied self-fertilisation and cross-fertilisation cases by fusion; and predict why interrupting the delivery pathway can prevent fusion despite successful pollination. Conditions and later establishment remain distinct from classification.
progression.nextLesson: the fungi, bacteria and protists contributions to `bio-m5-b02b` remain to be prepared and reviewed. They need their own named mechanisms and organism limits. After those group contributions, the existing canonical route points to `bio-m5-b03a` for mammalian fertilisation, implantation, pregnancy and birth, and `bio-m5-b03b` for agricultural manipulation. This plant contribution does not justify skipping the missing groups. Root decides the final focused playlist subdivision.
